title: The black panther
html_source:
Haines had experienced a nightmare in which appeared a black panther, whose terror he tried to end by shooting [destroying] it. Samuel Chenevix Trench, on whom Haines’s character is modeled, actually shot off a round from a revolver in experiencing the dream. The black panther, or leopard, is used several times in Biblical imagery. Jeremiah 5:6, for instance: “…a leopard shall watch over their cities: every one that goeth out thence shall be torn in pieces: because their transgressions are many, and their backslidings are increased.“ The “leopard” doing the watching is a Christ figure, the choice of “cities,” here Dublin, whose “transgressions are many, and their backslidings are increased.” The black panther is also, in Slovenian folklore a symbol for Deep understanding and spirituality.

In Gracious Wild: A Shamanic Journey with Hawks, Stacey L. L. Couch tells us the black panther is a symbol of darkness, not just because of the color, but also because, “Jungles are wet, messy, jumbled places and they mirror the unkept [sic] and unknown part of our unconscious. Black panther spirit animal is adept at navigating the unconscious, hidden parts of ourselves. She ventures into the unknown, comfortable with the darkness. Black panther spirit animal understands that the jungle is fraught with danger and rich with resources. The shadow is both good and bad.” She also delves into many themes from Ulysses as she asserts that, “Black panther symbolism is not only about traveling into our own darkness, but also the mystery of the universe. Both jaguars and leopards are solitary animals, and black panther spirit animal lends us the courage to venture into the unknown alone. The mystery of the universe is … the darkness of the womb, the place of pure potential creation… The void is a place beyond the five senses where we must venture on faith alone. The absence of moonlight makes black panther less visible and a superior huntress. The new moon is a time of both death and rebirth, when we stand at the threshold looking back at what was and looking ahead at what’s come. Neither are certain for this brief window in time. What was is no more and what’s to be is not yet born… The moon is strongly associated with the feminine as is the jungle and darkness, thus the black panther is said to carry the energy of the feminine principles of receptivity and intuition. Now is not the time for figuring things out or striking out, but for both turning inward to your soul and opening up to the Divine.”

The quote in the Oxen of the Sun episode complicates things further: “The black panther himself was the ghost of his own father.” Previous passages in which the phrase appears had clear references to Hamlet, and to Christ, whose father was referred to, sometimes indelicately, as the Holy Ghost. In Telemachus, however. Stephen hears his father’s voice as his own, for, as Mulligan has said, “he himself is the ghost of his own father.” This could infer that Stephen is either seen as another Irish victim, or, likelier (especially coming from Mulligan), a co-conspirator in Ireland’s destruction.
